casualties.source: Pusdalops-style coordination situation update, Monday 17 August 2026, 05:00 WIB, forwarded via WhatsApp and cross-checked by this SitRep against public BNPB statements
casualties.cross_check_note: The death toll (54) and its regency breakdown were cross-checked against Deputi Pencegahan BNPB Abdul Muhari's 16 August evening press conference (53 deaths: Manggarai 25, East Manggarai 20, Sikka 4, Ende 2, West Manggarai 1, Nagekeo 1, reported by Kompas and Tribunnews) — the 17 August figures are a plausible, internally consistent +1 (Manggarai 25→26) over that confirmed baseline, matching the steady overnight increment pattern (43→47→51→53→54) seen throughout this event. Aftershock, emergency-status-decree and press-briefing details in the same forwarded report independently checked out (see seismic_monitoring and emergency_status), which increases confidence in the rest of the document.
casualties.data_quality_flag: The East Manggarai (Manggarai Timur) injured breakdown in the forwarded report (3 severe, 21 minor = 24) does not reconcile with the last independently confirmed figure for that regency (21 severe, 59 minor = 80, from Abdul Muhari's 16 August evening briefing, cited by Kompas and Tribunnews). A drop of this size in an active response is unusual and looks more consistent with a transcription error in the forwarded message than a genuine revision. This SitRep shows the forwarded figure but flags it as unverified pending an official correction — the province-wide total of 204 is retained as reported since it is internally consistent with the report's own regency sum.
casualties.source_note: Deaths (47) and the 101-injured total are both from BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update. The 101 figure supersedes BNPB's earlier 113-injured figure. The 36 serious / 77 minor severity split still comes only from the Ministry of Health report dated 15 August (which totalled 113 injured and did not state a cut-off time). BNPB's 101 and the Ministry of Health's 113 are different counts from different agencies — do not add them together or assume one supersedes the other. These 16 August figures are retained below in casualties_by_location's deaths_bnpb/deaths_kemenkes fields for the historical record; the current top-level deaths/injured figures above are the 17 August update.

Sikka Regency.note: BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update revised Sikka from 3 to 4 deaths.

East Manggarai Regency.injured_pusdalops_17aug_flag: This sub-figure (3 severe/21 minor = 24) looks inconsistent with the last confirmed figure for this regency (21 severe/59 minor = 80, per Abdul Muhari's 16 Aug evening briefing) — see casualties.data_quality_flag.

Nagekeo Regency.note: BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update lists 1 death in Nagekeo for the first time; Nagekeo was absent from the earlier 18:48 WIB BNPB distribution. The Ministry of Health report separately lists 1 death for Nagekeo.

Manggarai Regency.note: BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update revised Manggarai from 24 to 23 deaths. The national total stayed at 47 because Sikka (+1) and Nagekeo (+1, newly listed) increased while Manggarai (-1) and Ngada (no longer listed, see below) changed. This SitRep treats it as a reported field revision rather than assuming which breakdown is more accurate.

Ngada Regency.note: Ngada appeared with 1 BNPB-attributed death in the 18:48 WIB, 15 August distribution, but is absent from BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August breakdown (which lists Manggarai 23, East Manggarai 17, Sikka 4, West Manggarai 1, Ende 1 and Nagekeo 1 — summing exactly to the stated total of 47 without Ngada). This SitRep shows Ngada's BNPB figure as not stated in the newer update rather than assuming it is zero; the Ministry of Health report independently still lists 1 death for Ngada, shown below.
Ngada Regency.deaths_pusdalops_17aug_note: Ngada is again not listed in the 17 August, 05:00 WIB death breakdown (Manggarai, East Manggarai, Sikka, Ende, West Manggarai and Nagekeo only). Shown as not stated rather than assumed zero, consistent with this SitRep's practice above.

East Flores Regency.note: No casualty report was available in the Ministry of Health table; East Flores was not listed in the BNPB death distribution.
East Flores Regency.regency_scope_note: The 17 August Pusdalops coordination report itself covers seven regencies only (Manggarai Barat, Manggarai, Manggarai Timur, Ngada, Nagekeo, Ende, Sikka) and does not include East Flores in its command/posko structure, though East Flores is connected to the response by the now-reopened Larantuka–Maumere road (see response_logistics).

displacement.status: More than 5,000 people displaced as of BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update; detailed site-level distribution is now available for three regencies.

Sikka Regency.detail: 1,356 people at the GOR Samador stadium shelter; 2,000 people self-evacuated across 10 sites.

cross_province_reports: Bima City and Bima Regency, West Nusa Tenggara (NTB) — see cross_province_impact
Kepulauan Selayar Regency, South Sulawesi — see cross_province_impact
displacement.note: The BNPB figures above are the first detailed, site-level evacuee counts published for this event; they supersede the earlier 'under assessment' status and the ~2,000 self-evacuated estimate, which is retained only as historical context.

damage.snapshot_status: Pusdalops-style coordination update, Monday 17 August 2026, 05:00 WIB (forwarded via WhatsApp, cross-checked by this SitRep — see casualties.cross_check_note). Figures rose substantially again from the 00:00 WIB, 16 August BNPB snapshot as damage-data collection was explicitly accelerated in parallel with the emergency response (see response_coordination, step 6).
damage.houses_damaged_methodology_note: Computed by summing the seven-regency breakdown in regency_damage_detail (Nagekeo, Ende, Manggarai, East Manggarai, West Manggarai and Sikka only). Ngada's house-damage count (1,796 units) is not yet split by severity in the source report — it is tracked separately below rather than folded into any one severity band.
damage.houses_damaged_ngada_note: Ngada's Pusdalops report describes 1,796 damaged houses as still 'dalam pendataan' (actively being assessed) with no rusak berat/sedang/ringan split yet available. This single regency's count is larger than the entire province's most recent differentiated total and is the largest driver of the province-wide increase — plausible given Ngada's more remote terrain and that BNPB's own directive called for accelerated, parallel damage-data collection.
damage.places_of_worship_note: Not explicitly restated in the 00:00 WIB source snippet available to this SitRep; the last confirmed figure (5, from the 17:00 WIB snapshot) is retained rather than assumed unchanged. The 17 August regency-level breakdown below reports facility damage per-regency but this SitRep has not re-summed a new province-wide total for education/health/worship/government facilities, since several regencies (e.g. Ngada, Manggarai Barat) report these as combined or still-being-counted figures — see regency_damage_detail for what is stated per regency.

total_houses_damaged_check.note: 1,634 (RB) + 400 (RS) + 711 (RR) across six differentiated regencies, plus Ngada's 1,796 undifferentiated = 4,541. This is a computed total for this SitRep, not a figure stated verbatim in the source report; the source gives only the per-regency breakdown in regency_damage_detail.

regency_damage_detail.status_label: Regency-level preliminary damage, Pusdalops coordination update, 17 August 2026, 05:00 WIB
regency_damage_detail.source_caveat: This table comes from a WhatsApp-forwarded Pusdalops-style report. This SitRep independently verified the report's casualty, aftershock and emergency-status figures (see casualties.cross_check_note and seismic_monitoring) and found them consistent with public BNPB/BMKG statements, which supports the credibility of this table, but the individual facility/road/office figures below were not each separately re-confirmed against another public source.

Ende.other_damage: 1 Koramil building damaged; 1 Polres dormitory boundary wall damaged.

West Manggarai.other_damage: 2 hotels moderately damaged; 1 KDMP building lightly damaged.

Ngada.houses_note: Still being assessed ('dalam pendataan'); no severity split available yet.

regency_damage_detail.abbreviation_key: heavy = rusak berat (RB), moderate = rusak sedang (RS), light = rusak ringan (RR) — Indonesian government damage-severity categories used consistently throughout this SitRep.

confirmed: BNPB recorded 47 deaths at the 00:00 WIB, 16 August cut-off: 23 in Manggarai, 17 in East Manggarai, 4 in Sikka, and 1 each in West Manggarai, Ende and Nagekeo — a revised distribution from the earlier 18:48 WIB count (see casualties_by_location for the full comparison).

The Ministry of Health report dated 15 August recorded 46 deaths and 113 injured people (36 seriously injured, 77 minor); its cut-off time was not stated. BNPB's 16 August update separately gives 101 injured; the two injury totals are not combined.

More than 5,000 people are displaced, with the largest concentration in Sikka Regency (3,356), followed by Manggarai Regency (2,078) and Nagekeo Regency (500); smaller numbers were also reported in Bima (NTB) and Kepulauan Selayar (South Sulawesi).

Province-wide preliminary damage as of the 00:00 WIB update: 914 houses heavily damaged, 126 moderately damaged and 317 lightly damaged; 93 education facilities, 36 health facilities and 38 government offices affected.

BMKG recorded 611 aftershocks by 02:00 WIB, 16 August, ranging from M1.9 to M6.2, with 16 above M5 and 30 felt by residents; activity was still concentrated in northern Flores and had not shown clear decay.

PLN reported 88% of affected customers in Flores had power restored as of its early-morning 16 August briefing, with 58 of 59 feeders (98.3%) and all 11 affected primary substations back in operation.

Badan Geologi (Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources) reported a preliminary, low-confidence indication of liquefaction (sand boils) at Waekokak, Mbay, Nagekeo, assessed as low-to-moderate impact pending field verification.

Manggarai Regency has formally declared a 90-day disaster emergency-response status (15 August–13 November 2026); NTT province was processing a 14-day provincial emergency-response decree as of the 16 August update.

At a 16 August coordination meeting in Manggarai Barat, BNPB's Head set out an eight-point strategic directive: same-day emergency-status declarations for six priority regencies, a posko command structure split between Labuan Bajo (national) and Maumere (tactical), a national logistics posko at Halim Perdanakusuma, Basarnas-led SAR, a 7-day basic-service restoration target with parallel house-damage data collection, cross-agency air/sea logistics assets, and daily 17:00 WITA media briefings (see response_coordination).
damage_reports: The 17 August, 05:00 WIB Pusdalops update puts province-wide house damage at 1,634 heavily damaged, 400 moderately damaged and 711 slightly damaged across six regencies, plus 1,796 houses in Ngada still being assessed without a severity split yet — a computed total of 4,541, up substantially from BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August snapshot of 914 / 126 / 317 (1,357 total). See regency_damage_detail for the full per-regency figures; Ngada's still-being-counted total is the single largest driver of the increase.

BNPB reported 93 education facilities, 36 health facilities and 38 government offices affected at the 00:00 WIB, 16 August cut-off, up from 87 / 18 / 6 at the earlier snapshot; the places-of-worship count (5) was not explicitly restated. The 17 August regency-level breakdown (regency_damage_detail) gives more current per-regency facility figures but this SitRep has not re-summed a new province-wide total, since some regencies (e.g. Ngada) still report facility damage as an undifferentiated, still-being-counted figure.

The Ministry of Health separately reported structural damage at 9 hospitals and 68 puskesmas (77 facilities total). This health-sector count is retained separately from BNPB's affected-health-facility figures because definitions and cut-offs differ.

Of the 50,000-package, 275-tonne presidential logistics commitment, the 17 August update reports a first sortie of 4,925 packages actually dispatched (3,200 via Labuan Bajo, 1,725 via Maumere), with a second sortie of 45,075 packages still planned. This is more precise than, and consistent with, the earlier 10,500-packages-arrived-at-Halim staging figure.

Manggarai Regency specifically requested 30 tonnes of rice, medicines, dozens of emergency tents, 1,000 folding beds, 1,000 blankets, 1,000 mats, clean-water tanks and generators, after its Bulog food-logistics warehouse was damaged; the 17 August update broadens this to a province-wide urgent-needs list covering tents, rice, bedding, kitchen equipment, water tanks, generators, medicines, ready-to-eat food, family/toddler kits and tarpaulins (see response_logistics.urgent_needs_17aug).

PLN identified 3,478 distribution substations and 11 primary substations affected; by its 16 August briefing all 11 primary substations and 58 of 59 feeders (98.3%) were restored, with 88% of affected customers back on supply and priority given to hospitals and airports.

Badan Geologi flagged landslides/ground movement, ground cracking, tsunami and a preliminary liquefaction indication as hazards requiring continued monitoring; a field team was dispatched to verify the liquefaction report.

Transport, road, electricity and telecommunications disruptions continue to be assessed; five airports and two ports (Reo and Maumere/Laurentius Say) were reported affected, and roughly 200 telecom towers (BTS) across 10 districts/cities were disrupted. As of 17 August, the Larantuka–Maumere land route has reopened while the Ende–Nagekeo route remains cut off (see response_coordination.update_17aug).
information_gaps: A single, reconciled evacuee total and full site-by-site distribution across all eight affected NTT regencies (currently detailed for three).
Reconciled casualty records across BNPB, the Ministry of Health, BPBD, Basarnas/QRSAR and district authorities — the Ngada/Nagekeo discrepancy between BNPB's two updates is not yet resolved.
Reconciled definitions and facility-level lists for BNPB's affected-health-facility figures versus the Ministry of Health's 77 facilities with structural damage.
Field confirmation of the preliminary liquefaction indication at Waekokak, Mbay.
Verified, earthquake-specific agricultural and livestock impact data from the Ministry of Agriculture (Kementan) — none has been published as of this update; see sector-impact.json.
Official monetary damage-and-loss estimate, and a reconciled district-by-district road/bridge damage list from the Ministry of Public Works (Kementerian PU).
disclaimer: BNPB's 18:48 WIB update is used for the consolidated death headline and its 17:00 WIB update for general damage. Ministry of Health figures are retained for injuries and detailed health-sector status, with the source's unstated cut-off shown explicitly. All figures remain preliminary and subject to reconciliation.

emergency_status.other_regencies_note: At a 16 August coordination meeting, BNPB's Head named six regencies — Manggarai, East Manggarai, Ngada, Ende, Nagekeo and Sikka — plus NTT Province, and urged them to issue emergency-status decrees that same day, stating the legal status is required before BNPB and other agencies can channel budget and technical support at full capacity (see response_coordination, step 1). As of 17 August, this SitRep has confirmed decree numbers for Manggarai, Ngada and East Manggarai (Siaga Darurat) above; West Manggarai, Ende and Sikka are reported as declared per additional_regencies_17aug but without an independently-sourced decree number; Nagekeo's status has not been separately reported either way.

tactical_posko.coverage: Sikka, Nagekeo and Ngada Regencies (eastern Flores)

national_logistics_posko.role: Central receiving point for assistance from ministries, agencies, state-owned enterprises, the private sector and the public, dispatched onward by air to Labuan Bajo and Maumere.
national_logistics_posko.cross_reference: See response_logistics above for package/tonnage figures staged at Halim as of the 15 August update.

posko_structure.regency_provincial_posko: BNPB's Head instructed rapid formation of regency/city and provincial posko, with TNI and Polri unit commanders serving as field commanders under one integrated command.

response_coordination.sar_command: Joint SAR teams (TNI, Polri, volunteers) placed under Basarnas' direct command until no trapped or missing victims remain — consistent with the sar section of sector-impact.json.

restoration_target.scope_note: Described by BNPB's Head as limited/normal function within 7 days, not full restoration.
restoration_target.parallel_instruction: House-damage data collection is to proceed in parallel rather than waiting for the emergency-response period to end, so temporary-shelter (Huntara) or repair-scheme decisions can be made as soon as figures are confirmed.

assets_deployed.focus: Reaching isolated areas to deliver food, blankets and tents.

media_center.purpose: Transparent day-to-day data updates intended to reduce misinformation.

steps.title: Accelerate formal emergency-status declarations
steps.detail: Urged the six priority regencies and NTT Province to issue tanggap darurat status decrees the same day, stating this legal status is required before BNPB, the Ministry of Public Works and other agencies can channel budget and technical support at full capacity.

steps.title: Stand up unified command posts (posko)
steps.detail: Regency/city and provincial posko to be formed rapidly, commanded by TNI and Polri unit commanders so evacuee management and logistics distribution run under one integrated command.

steps.title: National and tactical posko locations
steps.detail: A Main National Assistance Posko in Labuan Bajo (western Flores), commanded directly by BNPB's Head, and a Tactical Posko in Maumere (Sikka, Nagekeo, Ngada).

steps.title: National logistics posko at Halim Perdanakusuma
steps.detail: Centralised posko at Halim Perdanakusuma air base, Jakarta, receiving assistance from ministries, agencies, SOEs, the private sector and the public, then routing it by air to Labuan Bajo and Maumere.

steps.title: Basarnas-led search and rescue
steps.detail: Joint teams under Basarnas' direct command, with TNI, Polri and volunteers integrated under the Basarnas Head's leadership, continue SAR until no trapped or missing victims remain.

steps.title: 7-day basic-service restoration target; parallel damage-data collection
steps.detail: Target of limited normal function for electricity, clean water, fuel and communications within 7 days. House-damage data collection is to proceed in parallel, without waiting for the emergency-response period to end, so Huntara/repair planning can begin as soon as figures are confirmed.

steps.title: Cross-agency air and sea assets for isolated areas
steps.detail: TNI (4 helicopters plus ships), Basarnas (ships and aircraft) and BNPB (2 wide-body aircraft plus 1 helicopter) focused on reaching isolated areas with food, blankets and tents.

steps.title: Daily official Media Center briefings
steps.detail: An official Media Center began operating 16 August with daily press briefings at 17:00 WITA, intended to give transparent day-to-day updates and reduce misinformation.

response_coordination.scope_note: This directive sets out national command-and-logistics coordination structure. It does not itself set out sector-specific recovery plans (e.g. for health facilities); see health.json's recovery_targets for Kemenkes' separately reported hospital and puskesmas restoration targets.

update_17aug.source: Pusdalops-style coordination update, 17 August 2026, 05:00 WIB (forwarded via WhatsApp, cross-checked by this SitRep)
update_17aug.terminology_refinement: The 17 August report describes BOTH Labuan Bajo and Maumere as hosting a 'Posko Pendampingan Utama Nasional' (Pospenas / Main National Assistance Posko), with 'Posko AJU' (forward posko) also used for the Labuan Bajo/Maumere pair, and the Halim Perdanakusuma posko described as the 'Posko Logistik Nasional'. This is a slightly different framing from the 16 August directive's 'national' (Labuan Bajo) vs 'tactical' (Maumere) distinction recorded above. This SitRep preserves both framings rather than assuming the terminology has been fully standardised.
update_17aug.command_scope: This update states the response covers 7 affected regencies (West Manggarai, Manggarai, East Manggarai, Ngada, Nagekeo, Ende and Sikka), each directed to activate a Posko Penanggulangan Bencana led by its Bupati with Forkopimda, under NTT provincial coordination led by the Governor with Forkopimda. East Flores is not included in this 7-regency command list — see casualties_by_location's East Flores entry.

press_briefing_confirmed.status: The daily 17:00 WITA (16:00 WIB) Media Center press briefing announced in step 8 took place as planned on 16 August, with Deputi Bidang Pencegahan BNPB Abdul Muhari, Ph.D. as spokesperson — independently confirmed by Kompas.com, detik.com and Tribunnews, all citing the same briefing for the 53-deaths/135-injured figures.
press_briefing_confirmed.media_center_location: Main Media Center at the National Assistance Posko in Labuan Bajo, supported by the BNPB TV studio in Jakarta.

additional_coordination_meetings: A hybrid Rakor Percepatan Penanganan Bencana Gempa at the West Manggarai Regent's Office, 16 August 2026, 09:00 WITA, with Menko PMK, Menteri PU, Mendagri, Wamenkes, Wamensos, Kepala BNPB, Kepala Basarnas, the heads of PLN/Telkom/Pertamina, Pangdam Udayana, Kapolda NTT, the Governor and affected-regency Bupatis — this is the meeting from which the eight-point directive above was issued.

A coordination meeting convened by the Deputy Speaker of the DPR (House of Representatives) with the same set of ministries/agencies plus Manggarai's Bupati, 16 August 2026, 20:30 WITA, described as strengthening legislative-executive coordination on the emergency response.
update_17aug.infrastructure_access_note: The Larantuka–Maumere land route has reopened; the Ende–Nagekeo land route remains cut off as of 17 August, 05:00 WIB.
update_17aug.first_7_days_priorities: The Pusdalops update frames the first 7 days of the tanggap darurat period as prioritising: search and rescue; meeting basic needs; and the gradual restoration of infrastructure, communications, electricity, water, fuel and social services.

compiled_note: This SitRep was updated 17 August 2026, 06:30 WIB, incorporating a Pusdalops-style coordination update timestamped 17 August 2026, 05:00 WIB that was forwarded to this project via WhatsApp. Because the source was a forward rather than a direct official publication, this SitRep cross-checked its highest-stakes figures — the death toll and regency breakdown, the BMKG aftershock count, and the emergency-status decrees — against independently published BNPB/BMKG statements before publishing (see casualties.cross_check_note, seismic_monitoring.source, and emergency_status). All three checked out closely, which supports the credibility of the rest of the document; one specific inconsistency was found and is flagged rather than silently corrected (see casualties.data_quality_flag). Casualty, damage, seismic, emergency-status, logistics and command-structure sections were all updated in this pass; see response_coordination.update_17aug and response_logistics.sorties_17aug/air_fleet_17aug/shelter_and_medical_17aug for what's new.
